Dinesh Kumar Sharma Principal District & Sessions Judge/ Food Safety Appellate Tribunal Patiala House Court, New Delhi Fsat No. 06/2020 1. Sh. Raj Nath Bhat S/o Late Sh. P.N. Bhat R/o D729, Gali No.7 Ashok Nagar, Delhi92 2. Sh. Rajesh Dhingra S/o Late Sh. N.D. Dhingra R/o H. No. 92, Hargovind Enclave Delhi92 3. Smt. Poonam Dhingra W/o Sh. Rajesh Dhingra R/o H. No. 92, Hargovind Enclave Delhi92 4. Sh. Manik Dhingra S/o Sh. Rajesh Dhingra R/o H. No. 92, Hargovind Enclave Delhi92 5. M/s Narson Foods Pvt . Ltd. Plot No. 6, Parmesh ComplexII Community Centre, Karkardooma Delhi92 ...Appellants Versus Food Safety Officer Department of Food Safety Govt. of Nct of Delhi Fsat No. 06/2020 Page 1 of 8 8th Floor, Mayur Bhawan Connaught Place, New Delhi01. ...Respondent Date of filing of appeal : 25.09.2020 Date of arguments : 11.02.2021 Date of judgment : 11.02.2021 Judgment
texts.facts: 1. Vide this judgment, I propose to dispose of the present appeal filed by the appellants against the impugned order dated 06.03.2020, whereby the Ld. Adjudicating Officer/Additional District Magistrate (Shahdara), Delhi imposed a penalty of Rs.60,000/ u/s 51 of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006 (in short 'the FSS Act') upon each appellant. Sh. Raj Nath Bhat vs Food Safety Officer on 11 February, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85753783/ 1 2. The facts in brief are that on 03.05.2018, Sh. Pankaj Kumar Meena, Food Safety Officer took a sample of 'Butter' for analysis from the FBO/Appellant No. 1 at Plot No. 6, Parmesh ComplexII, Community Centre, Karkardooma, Delhi110 092. The food article was stored there for use in preparation of Shahi Paneer, Butter Roti, Butter Naan etc., intended for human consumption. The FSO tried to associate some public witnesses by requesting customers and passersby but none came forward. Thereafter, the FSO requested Mohd. Zubair, FSO to join the proceedings as witness, to which he agreed. At about 04:00 PM, the FSO purchased a sample of 'Butter' for analysis from the FBO/Appellant No. 1 and a credit note dated 03.05.2018 was prepared on the spot for payment of sample price but the sample price was not accepted because the article was not for direct sale. The sample i.e. about 800 gm 'Butter', which was ready for use, was taken from an open container bearing no label declaration. The sample of 'Butter' was taken after proper mixing of butter with the help of a clean and dry big spoon in a clean and dry steel container by rotating the same spoon in all possible directions several times. Thereafter, the sample of food article was divided into four equal counterparts and put in four clean and dry glass bottles, and thereafter 16 drops of formalin was added in each counterpart of the sample with the help of clean and dry dropper. Each bottle containing the sample was separately sealed as per the provisions of the FSS Act, 2006. Notice in Form VA was prepared at the spot and copy of the same was given to the FBO/Appellant No. 1. On 04.05.2018, one counterpart of the aforesaid sample of 'Butter' was sent to the Food Analyst. The other two counterparts were deposited with the Designated Officer Dr. Pramod M. Kothekar. As the FBO did not request to send the fourth counterpart of the sample for analysis to NABL accredited laboratory, it was deposited with the Designated Officer Dr. Pramod M. Kothekar. 3. The Food Analyst vide his report No. FSS/572/2018 dated 16.05.2018 opined that the sample is substandard because milk fat is less that the prescribed minimum limit of 80.0% and milk solids not fat exceeds the prescribed maximum limit of 1.5%. 4. The FBO was given an opportunity to file an appeal against the report of Food Analyst. The FBO preferred an appeal and one sample counterpart was sent to the Referral Food Laboratory, Ghaziabad (UP). The Referral Food Laboratory, Ghaziabad (UP) vide report No. 199/18/Jan/19 ND dated 17.01.2019 opined that the sample of 'Butter' does not confirm to the standards laid down in table below Regulation No. 2.1.10:1 of the Food Safety Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additive) Regulations, 2011, as the sample shows milk solids not fat above the maximum prescribed limit. The sample is thus substandard u/s 3(1)(zx) of the FSS Act, 2006. 5. Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, the Ld. AO/ADM imposed penalty of Rs.60,000/ upon each appellant u/s 51 of the FSS Act, 2006.
texts.arguments: 6. Sh. Kundan Lal, Ld. Chief PP for the respondent has submitted that the Ld. AO/ADM has rightly imposed the penalties upon the appellants, as the sample of the food article was found to be substandard. 7. Per contra, Sh. Sandeep Mishra, Ld. Counsel for the appellants has submitted that the Ld. AO/ADM has passed the order mechanically. It has been submitted that appellants purchased the Butter from Amul and therefore, the appellants cannot be held liable. It has been submitted that in Sh. Raj Nath Bhat vs Food Safety Officer on 11 February, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85753783/ 2 any case, Ld. AO/ADM has imposed very heavy penalty. It has been submitted that atleast the penalty may be reduced as the appellants are poor persons and already having no income in the Covid period. In State of Kerala Vs. Parameswaram Pillai Vasudevan Nair, 1975 Cri LJ 97, it was interalia held as under: "14.The Act is a piece of consumer legislation. It regulates to some extent the consumersupplier relations. Consumerists demand enforcement of discipline among the producers or manufacturers of food to ensure safety in the realm of food. The consumer's legitimate ignorance and his almost total dependence on the fairness and competence of those who supply his daily needs have made him a ready target for exploitation. The Act is intended to protect him against outright frauds. It does not provide for aggravation of offence based on the extent of contamination. The offence and punishment are the same whether the adulteration is great or small. Sh. Raj Nath Bhat vs Food Safety Officer on 11 February, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85753783/ 3 10. Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh (2019) 9 SCC 427, interalia held as under: "7.We are of the considered view that once standards are laid down by the legislature then those standards have to be followed. In items like milk which is a primary food, under the Act, it is not necessary to also prove that the food item had become unfit for human consumption or injurious to health. In cases of food coming under the Act, it is not required to prove that article of food was injurious to health.
